options.content:
Two streams, two questions. `ci:sign` files **Builds**, `job="supply-chain-build"`, when an image is signed and both attestations are attached. It shows what was *built*. **Inventory**, `job="supply-chain-inventory"`, is a nightly walk of the digests pinned in committed values. It verifies each SBOM from the registry. It shows what an environment *points at*, and a CVE asks that question.

This is a research surface, and not the incident path, per ADR-0501. Nothing here alerts, and nothing here links into the Overview funnel. Come here when you have a question, and not when a pager goes off.

panels.title: Images signed, 24h
panels.description: One for each signed image, across every service. A day with merges and none of these means that the publish pipeline stopped signing.

panels.title: Pinned images with a verifiable SBOM
panels.description: From the most recent nightly walk. A value below the total is an image that an environment pins, with a bill of materials that cannot be read. You cannot answer a CVE question about that image.

panels.title: Pinned images WITHOUT one
panels.description: The finding. A non-zero here does not page anyone; it means the next CVE question has a blind spot of this size.

panels.title: Packages in the largest pinned image
panels.description: Read from the verified SBOMs. It is not a health number. It shows how much surface one image carries, and how much a base-image change moves it.

panels.title: Signed builds by service
panels.description: Publish rate for each service. A service that stops appearing here while its code keeps changing is a service whose images are no longer signed. Admission notices it later, at deploy time.

panels.title: SBOM size by service
panels.description: Package count for each pinned image over time. A step change is a change of base image or dependency tree. It is the cheapest early signal that an image gained a lot of surface without a decision.

targets.expr: max by (service) (max_over_time({job="supply-chain-inventory", env=~"$env"} | json | unwrap packages [6h]))

panels.title: Build records
panels.description: One line for each signed image: digest, commit, ref, and the run that produced it. This is the audit trail. It shows when a digest was built and from what. That is why digest and commit are in the line, and not in labels.

panels.title: Inventory: images that could not be verified
panels.description: Each line carries the reason that cosign gave. So a missing attestation reads differently from a signature with a key that we no longer hold. Empty is the expected state.
